summary: Block. npm test passes 121/121, npm run check 11/11 and tests/bash-prose.test.mjs 14/14. Every bypass from a1 to a4-r1 is now denied (probe-r2 R1-R5). I compared the HEAD copy, verified identical to git show HEAD, with the working tree and confirmed the results in real bash 3.2 and zsh 5.9. Two single-call regressions remain. (F-1) dropFileHeredocs strips a trailing \r before it compares a terminator, but bash and zsh compare the raw line. A body line `EOF\r` therefore ends the heredoc for the guard only. Stacking a second plain heredoc lets a reset, a force push to main, a secrets read or rm -rf / sit in what the guard thinks is body, and all of them run. This breaks C-1. (F-2) joinOpenPush joins past the newline only when the push line holds a quote, $, a backtick, a parenthesis or a brace. An unquoted heredoc holds none of these. So `xargs git push origin goal/G-3 <<EOF` / `main` / `EOF` pushes main, --force or HEAD:main, in building and in done; HEAD denied all of these. This breaks the guards spec. Loop diagnosis: mostly the builder's fault, partly the critics'; the spec is not at fault. Each round's findings were real and were fixed as named. But the builder keeps answering with deny-lists of shell syntax (open characters for the push) and with leniencies the shell does not share (the CR strip, written in on purpose; see test line 141). Those cannot converge. The heredoc pass's own allow-list approach can, and both fixes below follow it. The a4-r1 and a4-r2 critics passed without probing how the shell parses the text, which let the loop run another round. The criteria are sound, so no human hold is needed. The a4-r2 critic's two notes are accurate and upheld; its pass is overturned by F-1 and F-2. Pre-existing gaps are recorded as F-4 (minor, preExisting).

findings.issue: dropFileHeredocs removes a trailing \r from each line before it compares the terminator (lines 75 and 84), but bash and zsh compare the raw line. In the text `cat > a.md <<'EOF'` / `x` / `EOF\r` / `cat > b.md <<'X'` / `EOF` / <command> / `X`, the guard ends the first heredoc at `EOF\r` and drops <command> as the body of X. The shell reads through to the bare `EOF` and runs <command>. A reset, a force push to main, a secrets read and rm -rf / are each allowed, all of which HEAD denied. A \r on the heredoc line (C5) and a tee variant (C6) work the same way.
findings.suggestion: Fail safe on carriage returns: return the text whole from dropFileHeredocs when the command holds any \r, rather than matching a terminator the shell does not match. Then change the all-CRLF allow case at tests/bash-prose.test.mjs line 29 to expect a deny, and add C1-C6 from probe-r2.mjs as denied cases.

findings.issue: joinOpenPush joins past the newline only when the push line holds one of the characters ["'`$(){}]. An unquoted heredoc on the push line holds none of them, so `xargs git push origin goal/G-3 <<EOF` / `main` / `EOF` is judged as a push of goal/G-3 only. xargs then runs `git push origin goal/G-3 main`. The same shape carries --force or HEAD:main past the deny pattern. All of these are allowed in building and in done; HEAD denied every one.
findings.suggestion: Replace the deny-list of open characters with an allow-list: keep the newline as the push boundary only when the whole push line, after global options are stripped, is `^[ \t]*git[ \t]+push(?:[ \t]+WORD)*[ \t]*$` built from the same WORD class the heredoc pass uses. Join every other push line through to the end of the text. Add the X4 shapes to the push test as denied.

findings.issue: This upholds the a4-r2 critic's note F-1: a heredoc body written to a git hook, a shell startup file or a path outside the project is no longer judged. C-1 mandates that for any file, and the Write tool can already write the same content to .git/hooks/pre-commit, whose content the guard never sees. The gap is not a regression of this slice. A later goal could judge bodies whose target is a hook or startup path.

findings.issue: HEAD and the worktree both allow the following. Global options missing from GLOBAL_OPTIONS hide the push from both the rule and the deny pattern (`git -P push --force`, `git --bare push origin main`). A combined short flag defeats -f\b (`git push -fu`). An alias set with -c hides push (`git -c alias.p=push p origin main`). `git push origin :main` deletes main in a dormant goal. A state file spelled `.HARNESS/state.json` or `.harness//state.json` passes the state guard on this case-insensitive filesystem. None of these comes from this slice.
findings.suggestion: A separate goal: list all git global options (or deny any push that has unknown options before the subcommand), match -[a-z]*f in short-flag clusters, treat a leading-colon refspec as a delete, and compare state-file paths after case folding and path normalization.
